question.leadin: Answer some questions about very badly named military operations.
question.text: Operations Breakfast, Lunch, Snack, Dinner, Supper, and Dessert were launched to bomb this country neighboring Vietnam during the Vietnam War.
question.answerHtml: Kingdom of Cambodia [or le Royaume du Cambodge, or Prĕəh Riəciənaacak Kampuciə; accept Democratic Kampuchea or Kâmpŭchéa Prâcheathippadey; accept Srok Khmae]
question.clue: The first king of this country's golden age empire was Jayavarman II, while its first constitutional monarch was Norodom Sihanouk.

swap.text: This woman, a Nobel Peace Prize winner, is the Prime Minister Elect of Burma. She has been under house arrest for most of the past two decades for opposing SLORC.
swap.clue: She leads the National League for Democracy, which she formed after the 8888 Uprising to protest against General Ne Win's dictatorship.

question.text: The accusations of Duterte "death squads" come from when he was Mayor of Davao City on this Philippine island, the main home of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front.
question.clue: Historically, the Sulu Sultanate controlled large portions of this island's Zamboanga Peninsula.

swap.leadin: This man fought his emotions while announcing the failure of a national merger.
swap.text: Name this founding father of an Asian city-state that became independent from Malaysia in 1965. This leader passed away in March 2015.
swap.clue: This man's government created the Social Development Unit, a state-backed matchmaking agency designed to reverse the effects of his overly-successful "Stop at Two" population control policy.

question.leadin: This regime established Democratic Kampuchea after winning a civil war against Lon Nol.
question.text: Name this regime, the subject of the 1984 movie The Killing Fields, starring debut actor Haing S. Ngor.
question.clue: This group forced city residents into agricultural communes in the countryside, and turned the Tuol Seng high school into Security Prison 21.

swap.leadin: This leader converted a high school into the s21 ("s-twenty-one") prison.
swap.text: Name this man, who called himself "Brother Number One" while leading the Khmer Rouge. ("Kuh-mair roozh")
swap.clue: Relations between this man's government and its Eastern neighbor deteriorated during his rule, leading to a Vietnamese invasion that ousted him from power.

question.text: Indonesia was ruled from 1967 until 1999 by this controversial president, whose support eroded after the Asian Financial Crisis. He established the New Order and took power in the wake of the 30 September coup attempt.
question.clue: He was propelled to power by the 30 September Movement, marking the end of "Guided Democracy" and the beginning of the "New Order" period.

swap.leadin: A rickshaw-like vehicle known as the becak was ubiquitous in this city before they were banned in the 1970s.
swap.text: Name this city whose skyline is dominated by the mortar-and-pestle-shaped Monas monument, which was built during the rule of Sukarno. It is the capital of Indonesia.
swap.clue: Government buildings are housed near its enormous Merdeka Square, which is home to the flame-topped Monas obelisk.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the Commonwealth's Pacific War.
question.text: British, and by extension, Commonwealth strategy for war with Japan revolved around this fortress-city whose heavy guns could only face the sea. The fall of this city in February of 1942 is considered one of the worst defeats in British history.
question.clue: HMS Prince of Wales led a naval group named Force Z assigned to protect this country that was destroyed by Japanese airstrikes prior to an invasion by Tomoyuki Yamashita's forces.

swap.text: General Vo Nguyen Giap surrouded the namesake French base in this decisive 1954 battle of the First Indochina War.
swap.clue: A three-day artillery bombardment by the victorious side preceded the two-month siege, which led the French artillery commander, Charles Piroth to commit suicide.

question.leadin: This invasion targeted 36 of the 44 provincial capitals of one polity, and led to a massacre at the ancient capital of Hue.
question.text: Name this North Vietnamese offensive which took place on the namesake holiday, also known as the Vietnamese New Year
question.clue: A picture taken by Eddie Adams during this military campaign depicts a man in a plaid shirt with a snub-nosed pistol to his head.

swap.leadin: Police in this city were referred to as "White Mice" by US soldiers due to their distinctive white helmets.
swap.text: Name this city from which American soldiers were dramatically evacuated on April 30, 1975. An iconic photograph depicts a line of evacuees attempting to board a small helicopter on the roof of this city's American embassy.
swap.clue: It's not in the United States, but a speech given in this city in 1945 begins, "All men are created equal. They are endowed by their creator with certain inalienable rights..."

question.leadin: Answer the following about Hindu kingdoms outside the Indian subcontinent.
question.text: This kingdom in modern-day Vietnam was surrounded by the Khmer empire and Đai Viet until it was annexed in 1471 by Vietnamese emperor Le Nhan Tong. This kingdom's king Bhadravarman I built the My Son ("mee sun") temple complex.
question.clue: Upon conquering the neighbouring Funan Kingdom, Shaivism became the state religion, and the kingdom was involved in the Spice Route as a producer of aloe.

swap.leadin: This country's Kayan people have been nicknamed "giraffe women" for wrapping gold coils around their necks.
swap.text: Name this modern-day country whose Konbaung ("cone-baong") dynasty outlawed the usage of peacock designs on non-royal clothes. This country's traditional longyi waist garment was inspired by Malay sarong.
swap.clue: In the 1400s, an enlightened king of this country used 294 tons of metal to cast a giant bell.

question.leadin: You are a hpaya kyun ("PUH-yah CHOON"), one of many indentured servants that tend to Buddhist monks and religious property. Answer the following about your life.
question.text: Your job is to clean religious buildings like this oldest stupa in the world. Dhammazedi's bell was constructed to be situated at this pagoda built around eight strands of the Buddha's hair.
question.answerHtml: Shwedagon Pagoda [or Great Dagon Pagoda; accept Golden Dagon Pagoda; prompt on Golden Pagoda or Great Pagoda]
question.clue: According to a legend, the merchants Taphussa and Bhallika founded this location after receiving eight pieces of hair from Gautama Buddha.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about early modern Thailand.
swap.text: This kingdom conquered Sukhothai to become the predominant Thai state from the 14th to 18th centuries, before falling to the Burman Konbaung dynasty.
swap.clue: Under its King Naresuan, this dynasty defeated an Eastern invader at the Battle of Nong Sarai.

question.leadin: In an iconic sculpture, this king is depicted pouring a goblet of water on the ground, showing that he no longer considered himself subject to the Burmese lords of the Toungoo Dynasty.
question.text: Name this great ruler of the Ayutthaya Kingdom, known as the "Black Prince," who was taken hostage as a child by the Burmese king Bayinnaung, only to return and reclaim his homeland.

swap.text: The second, or "restored" dynasty of this name, was the frst to re-unify Burma afer the fall of the Pagan kingdom and had its capital at Ava around 1606. The frst dynasty by this name arose in Burma under Mingyinyo near the end of the Ava kingdom and conquered the Mohnyin Shan peoples.

question.text: Along with the islands in the Labuan territory, East Malaysia is made up of these two states found on the north of the island of Borneo.
question.answerHtml: Sabah and Sarawak [order not important but don't accept or prompt on just one]

swap.leadin: In 1857 Chinese laborers revolted against one of these rulers after he instituted a high opium tax, and this dynasty had its capital at Kuching.
swap.text: Name this dynasty that controlled the Miri oilfields and ruled Serawak from the mid-1800s to the mid-1900s.
swap.clue: The Japanese invasion of Borneo ended the rule of this dynasty, which began when the Sultan of Brunei rewarded the patriarch of this family with the Raj of Sarawak after crushing a tribal rebellion.
